page: The Vultr voc-g-32c-128gb-640s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC architecture. It is provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, clocked at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction set extensions such as AVX, AES, and SHA_NI, while lacking AVX-512 extensions. The compute setup is paired with 128 GB of system memory, matching a balanced general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU, along with 640 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. No hardware GPUs are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multithreaded capacity and exceptionally high memory bandwidth. In memory subsystem benchmarks, uncached large-block read operations reached 537.96 GB/sec and write throughput achieved 292.8 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the top ten percent. Compute-intensive testing via stress-ng registered 99,997.49 in multi-core performance, mirrored by a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,165.0 and a Clang software compilation score of 42,736.0. In-memory data store performance is equally strong, delivering 73.66 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core (1,881.0) and single-threaded gzip compression remain in the average tier.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation ensures consistent execution without CPU stealing or noisy-neighbor contention. The integration of 640 GB local NVMe storage reduces external block-storage latency, providing balanced resource density across CPU, memory, and storage subsystems. The lack of AVX-512 and matrix acceleration units limits its utility for specialized heavy vector computation, but it delivers efficient multi-core density for standard parallel workloads.

The instance is suited for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, including continuous integration and software build pipelines, distributed database clustering, high-throughput Redis caching layers, web application backends, and multi-tenant container hosting.
